messages:
customer_jane: Hey team, we're seeing intermittent GitHub OAuth failures for mobile users. Error on redirect says 'state mismatch' ~10% of attempts after the last deploy. Can't repro locally.

alice_support: Sorry about the trouble — can you paste the exact redirect URI your app is using when it opens the browser / returns to the app?

customer_jane: Sure — this is what the app constructs: `myapp://auth/callback#state=st_xyz123&code=gho_ABCDEF&session=mobile`

jahyun_engineer: aha. fragments (the # part) never get sent to the server-side callback. If the app expects the auth server to echo the state from a fragment, that'll randomly fail depending on intermediate redirects. Is the OAuth client / proxy rewriting the redirect?

customer_jane: The flow is: mobile app opens GitHub auth in system browser -> GitHub redirects back to our public callback `https://auth.example.com/redirect` -> our redirect endpoint immediately issues a 302 to `myapp://auth/callback#...` with the code/state in the fragment. Some users hit a CDN/proxy that strips or normalizes the fragment. Logs show missing state on our redirect handler sometimes.

jahyun_engineer: That matches. When you 302 to a URI with a fragment, some intermediaries (and some OAuth clients) will drop/encode it. Also, fragments are client-side only — they won't arrive at our backend when the mobile app opens the final deeplink. The server should pass state in the query param to the final callback or persist it server-side keyed to the code.

alice_support: Quick repro steps we usually ask for: 1) exact redirect chain captured (curl -v follow) 2) response headers from auth.example.com 3) which CDN (Cloudflare/Akamai) / mobile browser and OS. Can you share a sample of server logs when this fails?

customer_jane: Here is one failing trace (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-10T14:02:13Z] GET /redirect?code=gho_ABCDEF
[2026-03-10T14:02:13Z] 302 -> Location: myapp://auth/callback#code=gho_ABCDEF&state=st_xyz123
[2026-03-10T14:02:13Z] INFO proxy-forward: upstream rewrote location to myapp://auth/callback
[2026-03-10T14:02:13Z] ERROR mobile-callback: incoming request missing state param
```

maya_infra: That proxy rewrite line is suspicious — which proxy version is in path? Some older CF worker rules will canonicalize Location and drop fragment. If you can point to an example request-id we can pull raw edge logs.

customer_jane: Request-id 01H7XYZ (sent via DM). Majority of failures are iOS Safari and some Android Chrome when going through corporate VPNs.

jahyun_engineer: Root causes / fixes:
- Best fix: Stop relying on fragments for state. Put state in query param when constructing the final Location, e.g. `Location: myapp://auth/callback?state=...&code=...`
- Alternative server-safe fix: persist the state server-side at the time you get the code and when the app hits the final deeplink, match it using the code exchange flow (associate code -> state on server).
- Short-term workaround: URL-encode the fragment into the path (not great).

alice_support: We'll also escalate to infra to check for any edge rewrite rules. @maya_infra can you grep edge logs for that request-id and confirm whether fragment was stripped at the CDN?

maya_infra: on it. quick note: fragments don't arrive at HTTP level, so proxies can't "strip" them unless they're rewriting the Location header. If your app expects the fragment, and your redirect server sets Location with a fragment, some intermediaries may rewrite Location and drop the `#...` part. I'm checking the worker rules now.

sre-bot: deploy:auth-redir-fix v2026.3.11 queued for canary, runbook: verify Location header preserves query vs fragment. :eyes:

tom_product: Also posting product note — many mobile SDKs recommend query param for PKCE/state to avoid this. We should add a short doc + quickfix snippet for customers hitting deeplink state issues.

customer_jane: Thanks all. We'll try switching the Location to use query params and test. Appreciate the fast triage.

alice_support: Please report back with results. If the change still shows sporadic state mismatches, we'll request raw edge captures and reproduce with a proxy chain. :thumbsup:
